principles: Only repair behavior when the code path can actually violate a requirement.
Use precise code annotations or truth-source narrowing for already implemented requirements.
Keep host-neutral authority: CLI/test/evidence are authoritative, Codex/Claude host outputs are advisory.
Avoid broad registry or optimizer-style rewrites outside the six gap set.
drivers: gap_analyze currently reports six high uncovered_requirement gaps and healthy:false.
Unsupported receipt algorithm is a production trust-boundary requirement and may need runtime fail-closed behavior.
Several Authority policy gaps likely reflect missing annotation linkage to existing implementation.
The user explicitly requires no arbitrary optimization and consistency of logic.

options.name: A: Minimal correctness fixes plus precise coverage linkage
pros: Targets only the six observed high gaps.
Fixes real fail-closed receipt behavior if missing.
Preserves existing worktree/planner behavior where already correct.
Makes gap_analyze convergence evidence meaningful instead of cosmetic.
cons: Requires careful verification to avoid mistaking annotation coverage for behavior correctness.
May leave broader gap_analyze heuristic limitations untouched.

options.name: B: Broad gap analyzer and metadata registry redesign
pros: Could reduce future false positives across more requirement patterns.
Might create a richer command metadata model.
cons: Optimizes beyond the current correctness issue.
Higher blast radius across process tooling and lifecycle gates.
Could obscure the specific production receipt fail-closed risk.

options.name: C: Documentation-only convergence
pros: Quickly resolves obsolete requirement wording if every gap is truly superseded.
cons: Would be unsafe if unsupported receipt algorithm is a real runtime gap.
Could make convergence look green without improving production trust-boundary behavior.
Does not satisfy the user request to solve the six high gaps robustly.

chosen: A: Minimal correctness fixes plus precise coverage linkage
rationale: Choose the minimal path because the gap set mixes likely linkage gaps with at least one possible production correctness issue. This keeps the story aligned with host-neutral Lattice evidence and avoids arbitrary optimization while still fixing real fail-closed behavior if present.

preMortem.scenario: We add keywords or annotations that make gap_analyze pass without proving behavior.
preMortem.trigger: Worktree/planner policy gaps are treated as text matching only.
preMortem.consequence: Project reports 100% convergence while runtime semantics could still drift.
preMortem.mitigation: Pair each linkage change with existing or focused smoke evidence and cite concrete runtime consumers.

preMortem.scenario: We overbuild ToolDef metadata and create a parallel command policy source of truth.
preMortem.trigger: supportsDryRun is implemented as a new standalone registry not consumed by existing command policy/help paths.
preMortem.consequence: Command semantics split across two inconsistent systems.
preMortem.mitigation: Either integrate narrowly with existing ToolDef/help/schema behavior or update the requirement to reflect COMMAND_POLICIES as the current contract.

preMortem.scenario: Unsupported algorithm is confused with subjectDigest algorithm prefix.
preMortem.trigger: Receipt tests only cover sha512: subjectDigest mismatch but not serverKey.algorithm or signature algorithm discovery.
preMortem.consequence: A production verification path may accept unsupported advertised key algorithms.
preMortem.mitigation: Add focused tests for non-ed25519 server key/discovery material and reject before verification can promote receipts.

preMortem.scenario: Host-specific reviewer output is mistaken for authority evidence.
preMortem.trigger: Claude or Codex says the plan is correct but Lattice evidence is missing or stale.
preMortem.mitigation: Record host reviews as advisory only; require lattice gap_analyze, focused tests, and lattice validate as authoritative evidence.
